To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
symmetry detection has a stronger effect on grouping when symmetry is redundant.
symmetry-based grouping is greater for redundant (i.e. more complex) than for simple symmetry and for vertically aligned endpoints than for horizontal alignment.

(1) redundant symmetry is a stronger grouping principle than simple symmetry, (2) the grouping effect of symmetry is stronger when symmetry is redundant (i.e., when it is carried by more complex elements), (3) grouping by symmetry is not limited to symmetry in a horizontal axis, but can also occur in vertical axes, and (4) grouping by symmetry can be measured by the degree of rotational linkage of two elements in common.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new measure of perceptual organization (grouping) and with a novel grouping principle, redundancy-based symmetry.
the effect of symmetry, a basic visual feature, on the process of perceptual grouping.
the influence of symmetry on perceptual organization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
redundant symmetry is a powerful grouping cue, and that the strength of the cue is a function of the probability of the symmetry’s occurrence.
the strength of grouping based on redundancy is greater than that based on non-redundant symmetry, but that the effect of symmetry is greater than that of other factors.
the effect of symmetry is a function of its redundancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the probability of an environmental arrangement of elements influences the degree to which that arrangement influences the grouping of those elements.
symmetry detection is a perceptual grouping mechanism that is influenced by the degree of symmetry redundancy.
redundant symmetry, like redundancy in general, is a cue that is more likely to be informative than simple symmetry, and therefore is a stronger cue for grouping.
The main takeaway from our work is that
symmetry detection is a complex process involving both the detection of symmetry in a stimulus and the weighting of the symmetry by its redundancy.
symmetry detection is a powerful perceptual grouping cue.
symmetry is an important factor influencing perceptual organization.
